newsitem.title: CHINA: China opens 'through train' service to Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: China opens 'through train' service to Hong Kong.

text.p: China launched a direct train service between Beijing and Hong Kong on Sunday as part of its bid to boost ties with the territory it recovers on July 1 after more than 150 years of British rule.

Vice Premier Wu Bangguo inaugurated the "through train" service by cutting a symbolic red ribbon and saying the new high-speed link, built over three years at a cost of 40 billion yuan ($4.8 billion), would contribute to Hong Kong's prosperity.

After a traditional Chinese lion dance, the clanging of cymbals and the blare of a brass band, the Number 97 train chugged out of the Beijing West Station at the start of its 29-hour journey across more than 2,350 km (1,410 miles).
Last September, China opened direct service between Beijing and Shenzhen near the British colony. Passengers had to walk across the border in a trip that took more than 40 hours.
The new service will carry passengers to the Kowloon railway station on Hong Kong's Kowloon peninsula.
"I'm really excited," said passenger Lin Junsheng before he boarded the train. "This is really convenient."
On Saturday, China auctioned gold and silver commemorative tickets for the inaugural trip. The highest bid for a set of tickets was 57,200 yuan ($6,890).
Many people in Hong Kong had once sought another type of "through train" to China, hoping the current legislature would straddle the transfer of power.
But Beijing, angered by direct elections in the territory, appointed a provisional body that it has made clear would replace the existing legislature at the end of British rule.
